clue.text: Get both sides all out, producing a no-win situation?

parts.note: to catch is to get hold of, and in cricket a catch gets a batsman out
two teams of eleven players, every one of them dismissed

explanation.surface: A fielding captain dismisses both teams and somehow nobody can win the match.
explanation.walkthrough: Catching every player in two cricket elevens means taking twenty-two catches. The question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from Joseph Heller's novel, where an absurd rule traps people so that every option leads to failure.

clue.text: Covering people with dung is reasonable

indicators.note: one thing covering another wraps around it, so the second word sits inside the first

explanation.surface: Spreading manure over a crowd is apparently a sensible thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: Compost is garden manure; the Latin phrase is the legal test of sanity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means of sound mind, so someone who is rational and sane in their thinking.

clue.text: Financial arrangement reportedly held in bond

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound of the phrase matters, not its spelling

parts.note: tied up tightly, as a prisoner or a chicken is

explanation.surface: A money arrangement is said to be held in a bond, as investments are.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond and arrangement both look financial, but bond here means a binding rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A trust is a legal setup where trustees hold and manage money or property for beneficiaries.

clue.text: Bloom's monster swallowing rage, almost

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: the many-headed serpent killed by Hercules

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of that word is dropped

explanation.surface: A flower is pictured as a beast nearly gulping down its own fury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloom's reads as Leopold Bloom of Ulysses, but Bloom is the definition and 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydrangea is a flowering shrub with large rounded heads of blossom, so it is a kind of bloom.

clue.text: Ruse for getting the last bit of vinegar into the seafood

indicators.note: putting something into another thing places it inside
the last bit of a word is just its final letter

explanation.surface: A cook's trick for squeezing the last drop of vinegar into a dish of shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: A winkle is a small sea snail sold at British seaside stalls, often eaten with vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a wrinkle is a clever trick or useful dodge, the same as a ruse or stratagem.

clue.text: Two sorts of vermin gaining energy from fertiliser

parts.note: a nit, the louse egg, and a rat
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Pests are thriving on the nourishment they draw from fertiliser on the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrates are nitrogen compounds spread on fields as plant food, a common kind of fertiliser.

clue.text: Tales of heartless sunbeam in the ascendant

indicators.note: in a down clue, ascending means going upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top
without its heart the first half of the compound word loses its middle letter

parts.note: split the compound: sun stays as written, and a beam is a ray

explanation.surface: Stories about a cold-hearted sunbeam climbing the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: Sunbeam must split into sun and beam; taking the whole word as heartless gets nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarns are long rambling stories, often exaggerated, spun by a storyteller.

clue.text: One girl crashed into former Liberal at the roundabout

indicators.note: going into something puts it inside the other word

parts.note: the Whigs were the forerunners of the Liberal party

indicators.note: something that has crashed is smashed out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A young woman drives into an old Liberal politician at a traffic roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: The roundabout is not a road junction but a fairground ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirligig is a merry-go-round or spinning toy, the playground or fairground sort of roundabout.

clue.text: The shape of decay

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a form or cast that gives something its shape
second meaning: fungal growth on rotting matter

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a gloomy phrase about how rot looks; really it joins two meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast or form gives an object its contour, and the furry fungus on old food signals rotting.

clue.text: Pause for popular pest cut short

indicators.note: cutting something short trims its end, so the last letter is removed

explanation.surface: Somebody stops briefly to deal with a well-liked insect that has been trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermit is to suspend or stop for a while, an old verb related to intermittent.

clue.text: Examiner, one holding up drunk male driver

indicators.note: holding something keeps it inside, so one word sits within another
in a down clue up means read from the bottom upwards, so the word turns round

explanation.surface: A driving examiner stops a drunk man at the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: The examiner holds the drunk upside down: TES(TOS)TER, then ONE. 'Holding up' looks like delaying traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Testosterone is the main male hormone, which powers sex drive and aggression, so it drives men.

clue.text: Away support in the wilds

explanation.surface: Fans following their team to a match far out in remote country.
explanation.walkthrough: The outback is the remote, thinly populated interior of Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Both name remote, sparsely settled country far from towns, the Australian term for wilderness.

clue.text: Forgive poet admitting backward look to verse

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so other letters go inside
a backward word is read from right to left

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for verse

explanation.surface: A poet pardons someone and lets them glance back at a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Dannie Abse was a Welsh poet and doctor; lo is an old word for look, as in 'lo and behold'.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to free from guilt or blame, as a priest pardons sins.

clue.text: Giant periodical covering game

indicators.note: something covering another goes around it on both sides

explanation.surface: A huge magazine has a cover story about a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are legendary giants, whose figures stand in London's Guildhall.
explanation.definitionFit: Magog is one of a pair of mythical giants from biblical and British legend.

clue.text: Old region revisited by boatman

indicators.note: revisiting something with fresh eyes changes how it looks, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller returns to a historic area, ferried by a boatman.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondolier is the oarsman who propels a gondola along the canals of Venice.

clue.text: Small plant may look lively

parts.note: to eye is to look at

explanation.surface: A little plant might appear perky and healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look lively' reads as a phrase meaning hurry up; it splits into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebright is a low-growing wild flower once used in herbal remedies for sore eyes.

clue.text: Dog inducing shepherd's delight?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an Irish breed of gundog with a chestnut coat

definitions.note: a phrase describing what the thing does, not a noun synonym
definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: a sun sinking crimson at dusk

explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'red sky at night, shepherd's delight' promises fine weather; a sun that sets red brings it.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed name is literally read as a crimson sinker, the sunset that the weather rhyme says pleases shepherds.

clue.text: It's unique, on average, in man

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: on par means at the normal standard

explanation.surface: An ordinary, average man is somehow also one of a kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The average goes in after the first letter of the name: N-ONPAR-EIL.
explanation.definitionFit: From French for without equal, nonpareil describes something matchless that no rival can equal.

clue.text: Spain's slender golden girl

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A slim, golden-haired Spanish beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor is a female given name, and crosswords treat any such name as a girl.

clue.text: Free ride cancelled at outset of long journey

parts.note: a lift is a free ride in someone's car

explanation.surface: A hitch-hiker's offer of a free ride is withdrawn just as a long trip begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift-off is the moment a rocket leaves the ground, the start of a voyage into space.

clue.text: Take the fizz out of the painter

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the French Impressionist famous for ballet dancers

explanation.walkthrough: The verb splits as DE-GAS, to remove the gas; the artist's name is spelt the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist artist, while removing gas makes a drink go flat.

clue.text: Identify one god and goddess

parts.note: Ate, the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to pick out a single deity and a female one.
explanation.walkthrough: Ate is a crossword regular: the Greek goddess of folly and rash action.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate a gene or cause is to single it out and pinpoint it, much like identifying.

clue.text: Singers bound head to foot

indicators.note: in a down entry the head is the top letter, and it moves to the foot at the bottom

parts.note: a leap or somersault, from Italian

explanation.surface: Choristers are tied up from top to bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: Bound looks like tied up but means a jump; a salto is a gymnast's somersault.
explanation.definitionFit: Altos sing the part just below soprano, so they are singers in a choir.

clue.text: Drink returned amid expression of contempt for perk

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one word sits inside another
something returned comes back the way it went, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A pint is sent back with a scornful snort at a work perk.
explanation.definitionFit: A freebie is something given at no cost, like an unexpected bonus or fringe benefit.

clue.text: Unproductive-sounding title

indicators.note: sounding points to how a word is said rather than how it is spelt

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads like a judgement on a useless honour; really one word is said like another.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is the lowest rank of the British peerage, so it is a noble rank someone can hold.

clue.text: Mean to crack the number of the games console

indicators.note: to crack something open is to break into it, so a word goes inside

parts.note: NO is the abbreviation for number
to mean to do something is to intend it

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to work out the serial number of a video game machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Nintendo is the Japanese company whose name stands for its video game machines, such as the Switch.

clue.text: Some of its sculptors obviously can't do heads

definitions.text: Some of its sculptors obviously can't do heads

indicators.note: some of a phrase is only part of it, so the letters are found inside the words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A joke that some sculptors are evidently hopeless at carving heads.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a statue of a body with no head or limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A torso is a sculpture of the trunk alone, made without head or limbs, as if its maker skipped heads.

clue.text: Tetchy allusion common in academic writing

definitions.note: a description of the thing rather than a noun synonym

explanation.surface: Scholarly writing is full of grumpy, irritable hints at other work.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer from one passage to another place in the same text, a staple of scholarly books and papers.
